implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) was approved 2026-09-15 (effective 2026-10-01) and covers IT, OT, and physical access accounts. OT account procedures for BAS Platforms A and B and the access control platform are due with the OT security standard (STD-02) by 2027-03-31.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Corporate and administrator accounts are created in the identity provider from the HR system feed and disabled automatically at termination. Tenant credentials are issued and revoked in the access control platform on tenant request. Gaps: local BAS accounts and security console accounts are not tied to the HR feed; about 1,900 tenant badges unused for 90+ days remain active; there is no tenant badge recertification; IT access reviews are annual (last February 2026). P07 found 4 of 25 sampled terminations with a local BAS or console account still active (POAM-001).
evidence: Identity provider export; badge activity report; BAS user lists; access review record February 2026

implementation_statement: Account creation, disablement, and removal for identity provider accounts are automated from the HR system (create, disable at termination, remove after 30 days).

Identity provider accounts inactive for 60 days are disabled automatically. Not implemented for BAS local accounts or for tenant credentials (planned: tenant credentials unused for 90 days suspended automatically, by 2027-01-31, POAM-001).
evidence: Identity provider policy; access control platform rule design

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Door access is enforced by door groups and schedules in the access control platform. Administrative access to the platform, the cloud accounts, and the BAS Platform A server is enforced by identity provider groups and platform roles.
evidence: Door group report; identity provider role export

implementation_statement: At Towers 1-4, OT zones are enforced by deny-by-default firewall conduits (SP 800-82 Rev. 3 zones and conduits), allowing only the historian feed, the access control and video cloud connections, and the remote access gateway. Gaps: P07 found a 'temporary' any-any rule from the Tower 1 corporate VLAN to the Platform A server left from the 2025 cutover (P01 R-050); Mixed-Use 1-2 door controllers and NVRs share corporate VLANs; Parks 1-2 and Retail 1-6 are flat (POAM-004).
evidence: Firewall rule exports for 14 sites; P07 reachability test

implementation_statement: IT administration and security monitoring are separated (MSSP monitors; IT administers). Gap: at Platform B properties the integrator both changes and approves BAS changes; no second reviewer.

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Corporate users have no local administrator rights. Gaps: 23 users hold full administrator rights in the access control platform (target: 6); Platform B uses one shared administrator account per site; 41 SCC and lobby users can export video (POAM-002).
evidence: Access control platform role report; BAS user lists

implementation_statement: IT administrators use separate privileged accounts in the identity provider and cloud. Not available on Platform B (shared accounts) until the upgrade (POAM-015).
Cloud organization root and identity provider global administrator accounts are limited to 3 named people with security keys; 2 break-glass accounts are sealed offline.
Identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts and alerts the MSSP. The access control platform portal and the Platform A server use identity provider sign-in.
A system use banner is shown at sign-in to the Platform A server, engineering workstations, and console PCs. Not shown on Platform B servers (vendor tool sign-in).
Console PCs and engineering workstations lock after 10 minutes idle, except the 6 SCC video wall PCs, which run kiosk-mode viewing accounts behind badge-controlled doors (documented exception).

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Access control and video portal sessions end after 30 minutes idle (vendor setting confirmed).

BAS Integrator A and the access control integrator use the remote access gateway in the shared services account: named accounts, MFA, per-session approval by a chief engineer, and session recording. Gap: BAS Integrator B uses an always-on vendor remote-support tool on the 8 Platform B servers with one shared account and no MFA (POAM-003).
evidence: Gateway configuration and session logs; remote-support tool inventory

implementation_statement: Gateway sessions are logged and recorded and sent to the SIEM. Integrator B sessions are not monitored (POAM-003).

Corporate Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication; guest Wi-Fi is isolated. Gap: at 3 retail centers the engineering tablet Wi-Fi shares the flat property network that reaches BAS controllers (POAM-004).
Engineering and security tablets are enrolled in mobile device management with passcode, encryption, and remote wipe; personal devices cannot reach OT networks.

Integrators may connect only through the gateway (Integrator A) or are under contract terms being added (POAM-016). Gap: Integrator B technicians connect their own laptops to Platform B engineering networks during site visits without a check.
POL-05 covers training; awareness and role-based training requirements are in POL-05 4.3 (approved 2026-09-15).
All 600 employees complete annual security training at hire and each year; quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 6.1%).
Insider threat awareness is covered in annual training for corporate staff. Not yet covered for SCC operators with video export rights (planned 2027-03-31).

No role-based OT training exists for chief engineers, engineering staff, or SCC operators. Planned: OT security training for 212 engineering staff and 40 SCC and lobby operators by 2027-03-31 (POAM-012).
POL-03 covers logging at policy level. The logging and monitoring standard (STD-03) that sets OT event types and retention is due 2027-01-31.

Event types are defined and collected for the identity provider, cloud, firewalls, gateway, and console PCs (EDR). Gap: BAS servers, network controllers, and access control platform administrator actions are not collected (POAM-006).
Collected records include time, source, user, and outcome. BAS Platform B logs record no user identity (shared account).

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews and alerts on IT sources 24x7 and reports monthly. No one reviews BAS or access control administrator activity (POAM-006).
The MSSP's SIEM correlates identity provider, EDR, firewall, and cloud events automatically.

Cloud and SaaS components use provider time sources; on-premises firewalls and the Platform A server synchronize to the shared services time service. Platform B servers drift (planned fix with the upgrade).
Cloud audit logs and gateway recordings land in a write-once log bucket in the shared services account; only the security team can read them.
Collected logs are kept 1 year searchable in the SIEM and 3 years in the locked bucket, per POL-03.
Audit record generation is enabled on IT components and the Platform A server. Not enabled on Platform B servers or network controllers.
The co-sourced internal audit firm assesses selected controls each year; the 2026 assessment covered 36 BAACS controls (P07).

Interconnections with the access control and video platform, the tenant app, the visitor management service, and the energy optimization service are covered by SaaS agreements. Gap: no written interconnection terms for the energy optimization service's write path into Platform A, or for the parking operator's LPR data feed (P10).
The POA&M (P07) tracks every weakness with an owner and date; the vCISO reports status to the audit committee each quarter.
The COO accepted continued operation of the BAACS on 2026-09-15 with the conditions in section 4.2 of this plan; the CEO accepted the High and Very High risks with dated treatment plans.
Continuous monitoring covers IT (MSSP, cloud posture service, monthly scans). OT has no continuous monitoring (POAM-006).
Internal connections among BAS servers, network controllers, and the historian are documented for Platform A only.
POL-01 and POL-04 address configuration at policy level; the configuration standard (STD-01) and OT security standard (STD-02) are due 2027-03-31.
Baselines exist for corporate endpoints, console PCs, and cloud workloads (benchmark-based). No baseline exists for BAS servers, network controllers, door controllers, or NVRs (POAM-007).

IT changes go through the change advisory process. Platform A integrator changes are ticketed through the gateway approval. Platform B changes are made by the integrator on site or remotely without tickets (POAM-007).
Impact analysis is done for IT changes and Platform A program changes. Not done for Platform B.
Corporate endpoints and cloud workloads follow benchmark settings with a monthly drift report. OT device settings are vendor defaults in many cases (P07 found default passwords, POAM-005).
Unneeded services are disabled on console PCs. Platform B servers run file sharing, a web interface exposed at Park 2, and the vendor remote-support tool (POAM-007, POAM-018).
IT assets are in the configuration management database. OT inventory covers about 55% of devices; P07 found 22 of 40 sampled Platform B controllers missing (POAM-008).
Planned: inventory updated through the change ticket for every OT device install or removal, and by passive OT discovery, by 2026-12-31 (POAM-008).
Users cannot install software on corporate endpoints or console PCs; application allowlisting on console PCs.
POL-03 covers contingency planning at policy level; the contingency and recovery standard (STD-08) is due 2026-12-31.

An IT disaster recovery plan exists (2024). Degraded-mode procedures for plant equipment and doors exist at Towers 1-4 only. There is no BAACS contingency plan covering Platform B, Mixed-Use 1-2, or the access control platform (POAM-009).
evidence: IT DR plan; tower manual procedures

implementation_statement: The IT DR plan is coordinated with the hurricane plan. OT procedures are not yet coordinated with the incident response runbooks (P08).
Planned: annual contingency training for chief engineers and SCC operators, starting with the tabletop on 2026-11-19 (POAM-011).
No restore test has been performed for the Platform A server, any Platform B server, or the historian. Planned: quarterly restore tests in an isolated recovery network from 2026-10-27 (POAM-010).
The backup vault is in a separate backup account in a second region, with separate administrator credentials.
Alternate SCC positions exist at Tower 3 but have never run a full shift; they use the same cloud video platform.
The towers have two ISPs and cellular failover for the SCC. Retail centers and office parks have one ISP each.

Nightly backups of the Platform A server and historian to the backup vault with 35-day write-once retention. Gaps: no backups of the 8 Platform B servers; field controller programs and graphics are held only by the integrators (POAM-010).
Planned: monthly integrity checks of backup sets and quarterly test restores (POAM-010).
Recovery steps exist for Platform A in the integrator's service manual; no tested reconstitution procedure for Platform B or for door controller reprogramming (POAM-010).
POL-02 sets identification and authentication rules for IT, OT, and vendors.

Unique identity provider accounts for all employees and administrators. Gaps: Platform B uses one shared account per site and a shared integrator account; 3 shared SCC video wall viewing accounts (documented exception) (POAM-005).
evidence: Identity provider export; BAS user lists

implementation_statement: MFA with security keys for identity provider, cloud, and access control platform administrators; MFA for gateway users.
MFA for all corporate users. Not available for Platform B local accounts (POAM-003, POAM-015).
Identity provider authentication uses replay-resistant protocols (number matching and security keys).
802.1X device authentication on corporate switches at the towers. Not on OT switches or at flat sites.
Identifiers are unique for staff. Tenant credential numbers are reused after revocation within 30 days (vendor default); change planned with POAM-001.

Identity provider passwords: 16-character minimum with banned list. Gaps: P07 found manufacturer default passwords on 9 of 30 sampled OT devices (Platform B controllers and 2 NVRs); the Platform B shared password has not changed since 2019 (POAM-005).
evidence: P07 default credential test; identity provider policy

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Tenant employees do not sign in to the system; they hold credentials issued after their employer's designated contact authorizes them. Tenant app users authenticate to the app vendor (outside the boundary).
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-09-15.
IT staff and the MSSP are trained on the IR plan. Chief engineers and SCC operators have had no incident response training (POAM-011).
Planned: OT ransomware tabletop on 2026-11-19 and access platform tabletop on 2027-02-17 (POAM-011).
IT incidents are handled by the MSSP and IT with documented steps. OT and access control incidents had no playbook before P08 (POAM-011).
All incidents are tracked in the security incident queue with discovery time.
Reporting duties are in the P08 notification matrix. The breach decision log and tenant notice register are not yet in place (POAM-021).
The MSSP and the insurer's panel forensics firm provide incident response help.
The 2024 IR plan covers IT only. The P08 runbooks add OT ransomware and access platform incidents with crisis management; they are approved but not yet exercised (POAM-011).
Platform A maintenance is scheduled and recorded through tickets. Platform B maintenance visits are not recorded.
Nonlocal maintenance by Integrator A and the access control integrator goes through the gateway with MFA and recording. Integrator B uses its own always-on tool (POAM-003).
Integrator technicians are named in the agreements for Integrator A only. Integrator B sends any technician.
Decommissioned drives and NVR disks are sanitized by a certified vendor with certificates.
USB storage is blocked on corporate endpoints and console PCs. Not blocked on engineering workstations, where integrators load programs by USB.
POL-01 and the facility security standard (STD-10) cover physical access to data rooms, engineering rooms, and network closets.
Access to the Tower 1 data room, SCC, and engineering rooms requires a role-based badge group. Gap: at Parks 1-2 and Retail 1-6, engineering rooms holding BAS servers use keys (POAM-013).

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Badge readers and cameras on the data room, SCC, and tower engineering rooms. Key control only at 8 properties (POAM-013).
The SCC monitors door alarms and video for data rooms and engineering rooms 24x7.
Visitor records for the data room and SCC are kept in the visitor management system for 1 year (lobby visitor records are a separate retention issue, POAM-017).
Policies POL-01 to POL-05 approved 2026-09-15 with annual review.
This plan, approved 2026-09-15.
POL-05 acknowledgment at hire and annually; integrators sign the rules of behavior before gateway access.

The OT architecture follows SP 800-82 Rev. 3 zones and conduits at Towers 1-4. Life-safety design rule: no network path from the BAACS to life-safety systems (section 7). Architecture not yet applied at 10 properties (POAM-004).

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: POL-01 establishes the program; the program roadmap is in P03. A formal program plan document is due 2027-03-31.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The IT Director is the designated information security officer; the vCISO sets strategy and reports to the audit committee.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Risk appetite statements approved by the CEO on 2026-09-15 (P01).
HR procedures cover screening, termination, and transfer.
Background checks for all employees, including security officers (state licensing applies to security officers).
HR records terminations before the last day; identity provider access is disabled automatically. Local BAS and console accounts and badges are not part of the workflow (POAM-001).
Transfers update identity provider groups; badge groups and BAS rights are not reviewed at transfer.
Integrator A and the MSSP have security terms. Integrator B, the guard contractor, and the parking operator have none (POAM-016).
POL-01 sets the risk assessment process (SP 800-30).
BAACS categorized Moderate (section 6 of this plan).
Annual risk assessment since 2024; 2026 assessment in P01 (50 risks).
Supply chain risks for integrators and platform vendors are in P01; no supplier-specific assessments yet (POAM-016).

Monthly authenticated scans of IT systems and console PCs; annual external penetration test (2026-03, OT excluded). No OT vulnerability assessment; P07 found 6 of 40 sampled critical IT findings past the 30-day target (POAM-014).
Findings are tracked to the risk register and POA&M with owners.
Critical components are identified from the BIA (P05): access control administration, SCC video, Platform A server, and tower chillers.
Security requirements are in new SaaS contracts since 2025. Not in integrator or guard contracts (POAM-016).

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: SOC 2 reports for the access control and video platform, identity provider, cloud provider, and MSSP are reviewed at onboarding; no annual review; AI vendors not reviewed (POAM-016).

Unsupported components: 8 Platform B servers and 5 engineering workstations on an operating system past support. Compensating: network isolation where present; upgrade planned by 2027-06-30 (POAM-015).

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Denial-of-service protection for the cloud platforms is provided by the vendors; property firewalls rate-limit inbound traffic.

Boundary protection at each property firewall and the cloud hub. Gaps: internet exposure of 2 NVRs and the Park 2 BAS web interface found 2026-07-21 (POAM-018); no OT zones at 10 properties (POAM-004).

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny-by-default at Towers 1-4 OT conduits and the cloud hub; the Tower 1 any-any rule found in P07 breaks it (POAM-004).

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Controller-to-cloud traffic for access control and video uses TLS; site-to-cloud VPN uses IPsec. BACnet traffic is not encrypted; segmentation compensates where present (AC-4).
Keys for the cloud workloads and backup vault are managed in the cloud key service with company-managed keys.

provider_if_inherited: Access control and video platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Vendor platforms use approved cryptography (TLS 1.2 or higher).
Cloud storage, backups, and console PC disks are encrypted. NVR disks are not encrypted; NVRs are in locked rooms (exception recorded).
Corporate endpoints and console PCs patched monthly. Platform A server patched quarterly by Integrator A. Platform B patched only at integrator visits; field device firmware not tracked (POAM-014).
EDR on console PCs, Platform A server, and the 6 Platform A engineering workstations, monitored 24x7. Not on the 8 Platform B servers or 8 Platform B workstations (unsupported OS) (POAM-015).
The MSSP monitors IT sources 24x7. No OT network monitoring and no monitoring of access control administrator actions (POAM-006).
The security team tracks CISA advisories, including ICS advisories for the BAS and access control products in use, weekly.
Platform A program changes are compared with the integrator's release copies. No integrity checking for Platform B programs.
Video retention ranges from 14 to 90 days by property with no written rule; visitor ID scans are kept indefinitely (POAM-017).
Planned: supply chain risk management plan as part of the vendor risk standard (STD-05) by 2026-12-31.
Procurement routes new OT and SaaS purchases to security review since 2025; integrator-supplied components are not reviewed.
Planned: annual Tier 1 supplier reviews (SOC 2 or questionnaire) beginning 2026-Q4 (POAM-016; P09 vendor-soc2-review.csv).
